text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The U.S. will provide $5 million to Pakistan for the import of wheat.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will address the nation at midnight of August 13 on the historic occasion of Pakistan's golden jubilee.
- The paramilitary Frontier Constabulary will take up security positions at foreign missions in Islamabad in about a week's time.
- Prime Minister I.K. Gujral has said India's sovereignty over Kashmir was not negotiable, but added he hoped relations with Pakistan over the territory would improve.
- In a major clean-up operation, police arrested over 150 criminals, mostly Afghans, from Khrotabad, on the outskirt of Balochistan province's capital Quetta.
- The State (central) bank of Pakistan has asked banks and financial institutions to prepare to take loan defaulters prromptly to court if they fail to take advantage of its incentive scheme.
- Citibank officials signed a syndicated loan of 4.5 billion rupees for Kot Addu Power Co Ltd, owned by Britain's National Power Company.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will inaugurate the Central Depository System at the Karachi Stock Exchange on September 3.
- Bidding for Ravi Rayon Ltd, a unit of Federal Chemical and Ceramics Corporation, will be held on August 12.
- Major oil producing fields in Pakistan have reached the brink of exhaustion.
- Exports rose 15.3 percent to $653.75 million in July from $567 million in July 1996, while imports rose 7.5 percent to $899.7 million from $837 million in July 1996.
- The Asian Development Bank will release the first tranche of a short-term $250 million loan by October provided Pakistan formalises an agreement with the IMF.
